surfaces.part: spine and back ridge with snow highlights
ribcage and torso, drawn in side profile

answer.evidence: This is a standing mammoth skeleton seen in flat side elevation, facing east with the tusk on the right. The spine and ribs are a profile silhouette. The white snow on the back ridge (rows 12-31) follows the outline and has no front-edge line or eave shadow, so it is not a horizontal top surface. The ribs are see-through vertical bars. The legs stand on two snow patches (rows 53-59), which I counted as decor rather than a top of the main body. No part of the main body shows a top surface. The object is also an upright articulated skeleton, not scattered floor debris, so the kind fits poorly.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 14 visible tones per 16x16 tile, within the references' 9-20 range and close to the stall (17) and well (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no big flat fills. The bone ramp reads as about 4 steps (bright highlight, cream, pinkish shadow, dark maroon), a little below the 5-6 of the references. The outline is partly tinted and partly neutral (43% near-neutral, similar to the bench at 44% and the well at 33%), so I call it mixed. The edges lean dark red-brown beside the bone and are not a uniform black sticker line. The ribs, spine knobs, skull and tusks carry per-bone shading and small gaps of value. The cloud-like white puffs under the feet are a slightly odd base, but they are shaded, not flat. A careful artist would accept it beside the references without it looking flatter or thinner.
